### failure_allocation

### quantity_and_thickness

Capacity scales with represented volume, so twice the plate takes about twice the hits. Doubling the represented thickness doubles the load-bearing area and halves the stress, so a hit that dents the thin plate stays recoverable on the thick one.

### resting_support

A safe resting load charges nothing however long it rests. An overload yields and charges plateau work each tick until the plank fails in bounded time, sooner for a larger overload; a host-measured plastic displacement replaces the fallback progression.

### partition

Splitting one contact into equivalent colliders must not multiply energy. Merged sub-contacts reproduce the single contact exactly; charging each part with the whole event would overstate the damage several times over.

### fixed_step

The plank press and a connection moment just past their safe limits, stepped at 30, 60, 120 and 240 Hz, where 240 Hz is the 60 Hz tick with four substeps. Constant-strength fallback work integrates linearly. Cumulative work and integrity after 1/30 s match at every rate; failure lands within one tick (plus f32 rounding) of the analytic time. Event columns describe only the tick ending at 1/30 s; cumulative work is explicitly separate.
